models.name: Water Molecule
models.author: MehdiMM
models.note: Ball-and-stick illustration of H2O. Sphere radii and bond thickness are illustrative; the listed length is the molecular span.

models.name: Glucose Molecule
models.author: brutebandit
models.note: Molecular illustration, not an electron-density surface. The longest visible axis is used as an approximate span.

models.name: DNA Helix Width
models.author: alexanderesmith
models.note: An atom-colored segment of human B-DNA with alternating A–T and C–G pairs, credited to alexanderesmith. The listed 2 nm measures double-helix width, not the length of this arbitrary segment; hydrogen is white, oxygen red, nitrogen blue, carbon gray, and phosphorus yellow.

models.name: Protein (Small)
models.author: sduce
models.note: A human insulin monomer, not an interchangeable model of every small protein. The listed 5 nm is a representative protein scale, not a measured diameter of this conformer; its longest visible mesh extent is normalized to that illustrative value.

models.name: Bacteria
models.author: andrewfrueh
models.note: A rod-shaped bacterium bristling with short pili, in a muted teal (E. coli has no natural color; this is an illustration convention). Its body is calibrated to the listed 2 micrometer length of E. coli. Its flagella are shortened to fit the explorer; real E. coli flagella trail several times the body length.

models.name: Red Blood Cell
models.author: elearning.imu
models.note: Biconcave red blood cell from an educational morphology model. The listed size refers to cell diameter.

models.name: Ant
models.author: 3d-render.nl
models.note: Representative black ant; body lengths differ greatly among ant species.

models.name: Housefly
models.author: Schmoldt5000
models.note: Adult Musca domestica with anatomically recognizable body, legs and wings. The source display pedestal is excluded. Its body-axis extent is an approximate proxy for the listed body length, not a measured specimen.

models.name: Butterfly Wingspan
models.author: victorberdugo1
models.note: Open-wing monarch illustration. The wingtip-to-wingtip mesh extent represents the listed wingspan.

models.name: Human Height
models.author: renderpeople
models.note: Photogrammetry-style 3D scan of a real adult man standing naturally (Renderpeople 'Dennis Posed 004', published CC BY 4.0 by Renderpeople): fully textured, wearing a suit, one hand in a pocket, no nudity. The calibrated height is the full vertical extent from shoe soles to the top of the hair, scaled to the representative 1.7 m, so it is not a measurement of the scanned person (the source scan stands about 1.87 m). Original 8k textures reduced to 1024 px; geometry kept at about 100k triangles.

models.name: Cat Length
models.author: rt699448
models.note: User-selected domestic cat; the 46 cm dataset length is nose to rump and excludes the visible tail. The modeled body is estimated as 84% of the source mesh's longest bound.

models.name: Giraffe Height
models.author: BlueMesh
models.note: Representative standing giraffe. The model is scaled by height, not claimed to depict a measured individual.

models.name: Blue Whale
models.author: ostapblendercg
models.note: Textured adult blue-whale illustration, selected for a recognizable side silhouette. The dataset value is a representative body length.

models.name: Eiffel Tower
models.author: Lambo_SC04
models.note: User-selected lattice Eiffel Tower; vertical mesh height represents the listed 330 m landmark height.

models.name: Burj Khalifa
models.author: noears6
models.note: Architectural illustration of Burj Khalifa. The listed dimension is total building height.

models.name: Football Field
models.author: johnnokomis
models.note: A drone photogrammetry scan of the football field at Milton Frank Stadium in Huntsville, Alabama, cropped to the playing surface; stands, track, lights, and the noisily scanned goalposts were removed. The goal-line-to-goal-line span, 100 yards (91.44 m), is calibrated to the listed length; it is about three quarters of the mesh, which also includes both end zones and a strip of turf beyond them.

models.name: Statue of Liberty
models.author: e-sfera (skolskaknjiga)
models.note: e-sfera's authored model of the whole monument: the copper statue on Richard Morris Hunt's granite pedestal, standing inside the star-shaped walls of Fort Wood. Its full height, from the ground at the fort to the torch, is calibrated to the listed 92.99 m; in the model the statue is half of that height, matching the real 46.05 m statue on 46.94 m of pedestal and foundation. Details are simplified for a low-poly model.

models.name: Boeing 747-8
models.author: jsong.js.us
models.note: Authored Boeing 747-8 Intercontinental model by AF267 (jsong.js.us), originally configured for GeoFS. Calibrated uniformly nose to tail to the catalog’s 76.3 m overall length. The model’s span-to-length ratio is about 0.898, close to Boeing’s 68.4/76.3; local details, livery and landing gear are illustrative rather than an engineering survey. No geometry is stretched independently.

models.name: Elephant Bird Egg
models.author: RISDNaturelab
models.note: Real surface scan of RISD Nature Lab accession 132.32, reassembled from eggshell fragments and presumed by the collection to be an elephant-bird egg. Uniformly calibrated to the catalog’s representative 33 cm long axis, not a measured dimension or confirmed species identification of this particular specimen. Scan cracks and repaired fragments are retained; no invented shell geometry.

models.name: Hindenburg
models.author: hank2
models.note: Authored Hindenburg airship by hank2, uniformly calibrated to 245 m overall length. Envelope, gondolas, fins and historically contextual tail markings are retained. The neutral envelope material is lightened for legibility; no independent axis scaling. Internal framework and gas bags are the artist’s illustration, not a structural survey.

models.name: Komodo Dragon
models.author: denys4624
models.note: Authored Komodo dragon illustration by denys4624, uniformly calibrated nose to tail to the catalog’s representative 2.6 m adult-male length. The extended tail is included. This is an artist’s animal, not a scan, measured specimen or anatomical reconstruction; surface details and pose are illustrative.

models.name: Sperm Whale
models.author: AneesAnimates
models.note: Sperm-whale exterior illustration by AneesAnimates, not a specimen scan or a measured individual. The original neutral bind pose is frozen, rigidly transformed and uniformly scaled nose to fluke to the catalog’s 52 ft (15.8496 m) representative male length from NOAA. The source has no base-color map; gray-blue skin color is authored for this display. Source normal/roughness maps and sculpted wrinkles are retained; their local detail is illustrative rather than measured anatomy. The rig and animations are removed after baking joint transforms; the delivered model is static and remains freely rotatable. CC BY 4.0; adaptation by Universe Scales.

models.name: African Bush Elephant
models.author: jimmyho905
models.note: African-elephant exterior illustration by jimmyho905, uniformly calibrated to the catalog’s 3.2 m representative adult-male shoulder height. In this neutral pose the highest mesh point is the dorsal withers above the forelegs; the head, ears and trunk are lower, so the Y extent measures foot to shoulder rather than body length or head height. A predominantly frontal resting view preserves the shoulder-height size comparison; drag to inspect the whole, longer body. The artist identifies the model as African Elephant; this is an illustrative savanna-elephant appearance, not a specimen scan, verified individual or measured male. Source geometry and textures are retained, the neutral skin bind pose is baked and the rig removed, and tangents are regenerated. No independent-axis scaling, shortened body or cropped anatomy. CC BY 4.0; adaptation by Universe Scales.

models.name: Chloroplast
models.author: montanhabio
models.note: Authored chloroplast cutaway by montanhabio, uniformly calibrated to the representative 5 µm long axis. The model shows envelope, thylakoid stacks and stromal connections with DNA indicated. It is a teaching illustration, not segmented EM or measured internal architecture. Green/gold false colours were added and the floating title removed. Internal proportions and disc counts are illustrative.

models.name: Rotifer
models.author: .hapto
models.note: A bdelloid rotifer illustration by .hapto GmbH for Senckenberg’s soil-life project, uniformly calibrated corona-to-toes to the catalog’s representative 200 µm length. The paired ciliated corona and telescoping body are authored anatomy, not a scan or an identified measured specimen. Original painted colours are retained in a light-responsive material; the cilia are static.

models.name: Human Eye
models.author: maskutfab
models.note: Authored external human-eye illustration by ScannerDev (maskutfab), uniformly calibrated to a representative 24 mm transverse eyeball diameter. The source sclera, iris, pupil and corneal surface are retained with their textures. It is not a patient scan or an optical/vascular reconstruction; the painted vessels are illustrative and no internal anatomy is claimed.

models.name: Honeybee
models.author: etainproject
models.note: ETAIN / Arno Thielens worker honeybee micro-CT surface, in native millimetres. Its approximately 11 mm body is preserved within the catalog’s representative 12.5 mm scale, rather than enlarged to fill it. The preserved compact pose and unresolved/absent wing and leg detail remain as in the scan; no flying pose, hair or missing appendages are invented. Amber false colour is for inspection, not measured pigmentation.

models.name: Hyperion
models.author: rhcreations
models.note: Redwood illustration by rhcreations, uniformly scaled base to crown to the current catalog’s 116.2 m Hyperion height (the brief gives 116.22 m). It is a generic redwood tree model, not a scan, reconstruction, crown map or girth measurement of Hyperion. The shape, branch structure and foliage are authored; transparent foliage cards are retained as alpha-tested double-sided surfaces. The source’s legacy specular/glossiness materials are converted to metallic/roughness. Guinness documents 116.07 m in 2019; that older measurement does not independently verify the current 2026 catalog figure. No exact location is included.

models.name: Titanic
models.author: farhad.Guli
models.note: Authored RMS Titanic exterior by farhad.Guli, uniformly calibrated bow to stern to the catalog’s 269.1 m overall length (882 ft 9 in is 269.0622 m). Hull, four funnels, superstructure and source rigging are retained. This is an artist’s ship, not a scan or engineering reconstruction; local proportions, colors, deck fittings and rigging are illustrative. Simplification retains source linework as well as triangle meshes. No waterline crop, sinking pose or wreck geometry is introduced.

models.name: Bacteriophage T4
models.author: andresfranciscosanchez13
models.note: An artist's model of bacteriophage T4 (andresfranciscosanchez13, CC BY 4.0): the icosahedral head that holds its DNA, the contractile tail sheath and the six long tail fibers that grab a bacterium. Scaled so head through tail is the listed 200 nanometers; the fibers reach below the baseplate. Illustrative shapes and colors, not a structure determination; the source's display platform was removed.

models.name: Mimivirus
models.author: AH (agher)
models.note: An artist's model of a mimivirus particle (AH, CC BY 4.0): a capsid of repeated protein units bristling with surface fibers, scaled so its full width including the fibers is the listed 600 nanometers, larger than some bacteria. Illustrative, not a structure determination.

models.name: Fruit Fly
models.author: etainproject
models.note: Female Drosophila melanogaster micro-CT scan from the ETAIN project; reared in the Wijnen lab at the University of Southampton, scanned by Orestis Katsamenis and processed by Felipe Ribas. The source scan geometry, orange CT material and preserved-specimen pose are retained. Uniformly scaled between head and abdomen-tip surface landmarks to the catalog’s representative 2.5 mm body length; legs, wings and bristles extend beyond that measurement. This is a stained, fixed laboratory specimen, not natural surface coloration or a living flight pose.

models.name: Tyrannosaurus Rex SUE
models.author: rigsters
models.note: Photogrammetry scan by Rigsters of a Tyrannosaurus rex skeleton replica displayed at Knuthenborg Safaripark, Denmark. This is a different replica, not SUE or a scan of SUE’s fossils; it is uniformly scaled to the catalog’s approximate 12.3 m length using the skull-to-tail longitudinal extent. The replica’s pose and proportions are retained. A rapid single-loop capture leaves holes and incomplete surfaces, especially visible from the reverse side; these have not been filled with invented bones or surfaces.

models.name: Basketball
models.author: robin.sculac
models.note: Photogrammetry of a worn Spalding basketball by robin.sculac, captured with 3DF Zephyr. The photographed seams, pebbling, printed markings and wear replace the original dimensioned illustration. The source does not identify its ball size or supply a measured diameter: this specimen is uniformly calibrated to the catalog’s representative 239 mm diameter, rather than claimed to be a measured size-7 ball. Source proportions, colors and scan irregularities are retained; no surface was filled, reshaped or generated.

models.name: International Space Station
models.author: calebcram
models.note: Textured low-poly model of the International Space Station by calebcram: the integrated truss with its solar array wings, radiators and pressurized modules. It is an artist's game-ready model, not an engineering mesh; its longest span, the truss, is uniformly calibrated to the catalog's 109 m end-to-end length.
